walkthroughs.body_html:
UK's largest national park, NW England. Classic glacial scenery: ribbon lakes (Windermere, Ullswater), U-shaped valleys, corries, England's highest peak Scafell Pike (978m).

UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017. Around 18 million visitors per year.

Tourism: hotels, cafes, boat hire, climbing — biggest employer.

Hill sheep farming: Herdwick sheep — vital for landscape and culture.

Forestry: conifer plantations e.g. Whinlatter, Grizedale.

Quarrying: slate quarries at Honister.

Traffic: narrow lanes jammed in summer.
Footpath erosion: hills like Helvellyn worn bare.
House prices: second homes price out locals.
Farming vs tourism: walkers and dogs disturb livestock.

Solutions: Fix the Fells path repairs, park-and-ride, affordable housing schemes, off-season marketing.

mcqs.q: How does an oxbow lake form from a meander?
options: Oxbow lakes form when meanders dry up completely.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Erosion on outside bends narrows the meander neck; during a flood the river cuts across the neck, deposition seals the old loop, leaving a horseshoe-shaped lake.
Oxbow lakes form where two rivers meet and one stops flowing.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.

mcqs.q: What is hydraulic action in a river?
options: Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
The force of moving water itself compressing air into cracks in the river bank or bed, weakening rock until pieces break off — no sediment needed.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Hydraulic action is when rocks in the river smash into each other.
